Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks for the clear questions — below is a concise summary of Redwood's standard posture. Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through specifics.

1) Deletion SLA (live data, caches, indexes)
- Standard: Customer-initiated deletion requests are propagated and data is removed from primary (live) storage within 30 days by default. This includes removal from user-visible indexes and standard caches.
- Ephemeral K/V caches: TTL-style caches are cleared on deletion requests, but depending on in-flight requests there may be short-lived residuals; we aim for functional deletion within 24-72 hours for active caches.
- Enterprise option: Accelerated deletion (e.g., 7-day SLA) is available under contract for enterprise customers with higher fees and controls.

2) Backups
- Backups may contain customer data necessary for disaster recovery. Default full-snapshot retention is 90 days.
- Deletion propagation: Backup snapshots are treated as immutable during their retention window; standard deletion requests do not retroactively remove data from already-captured immutable snapshots.
- Options: We offer (a) shorter retention windows for backups, (b) customer-managed snapshot lifecycle via dedicated S3 buckets (recommended for regulated customers), and (c) contractual carve-outs where we agree to accelerated backup purging for an additional compliance fee.

3) Logs & telemetry
- Standard retention: request/trace logs are retained for 90 days. Aggregated metrics and anonymized usage stats are retained longer (configurable).
- Pseudonymization: Logs can be configured to redact or pseudonymize user identifiers at ingest. We recommend pseudonymization when customers require limited-identifiability logs for debugging.
- Audit logs: Admin/audit logs are retained per service tier; longer retention windows available as an add-on.

4) SOC 2 / HIPAA
- SOC 2 Type II: Redwood currently has an active SOC 2 Type II report (period: 2025-07 to 2026-07). We can share the report under NDA.
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA-controlled workloads via a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). We have customer references and standard BAA language — execution required prior to PHI processing.

5) Practical notes and recommended next steps
- If Amaya needs deletions that remove data from past immutable backups, we recommend customer-managed backup storage or an explicit contractual SLA for backup purging.
- For logs, we can enable a pseudonymization pipeline during onboarding to reduce re-identifiability.
- I'll attach the security brief and the checklist answers for the questionnaire — Marissa, please share with Sam/Priya.

If you want, I can join the vendor questionnaire session next week to answer any live follow-ups.
